story.magic_realms.marcus_thorpan.title: Marcus Thorpan, the Ilisiitsoq
story.magic_realms.marcus_thorpan.chapte: Angakkuq

My name is Marcus Thorpan, and I was the Angakkuq of a remote Inuit village, their master of frost. My life was simple; I lived to protect the villagers from the biting cold and the unusual monsters that roamed the perimeter.
I was their only shield in that ferocious environment, and I believed my magic was enough to keep the unforgiving mountains at bay. I was a fool.

In the frozen peaks, there are monsters that hide from the exterior not out of fear, but because they have no need to surface. The true horrors begin when they finally decide to leave their dens. That is when I learned that as powerful as I thought I was, it was nothing compared to the nightmares hiding beneath the frosted dunes.
The Ruined Village

I remember the night it began, though the omens were there days earlier. During a routine patrol through the frozen pine forest, I found a gruesome trail of carcasses: caribou, wolves, even massive snow bears. All of them were dead, and every single one had been cleanly beheaded. I foolishly dismissed it as the work of some strange new predator. I did not realize it was a prelude to the end.

On the distant horizon, grotesque silhouettes took shape in the dark: ice spiders. They were monsters I had never seen before, but I did not need to study them to know the disaster they would cause. When the swarm of ice spiders finally arrived at the village, my frost proved useless against them; they were born of the cold, and my magic simply washed over their shells.

For two agonizing days, I fought them in the village square. When the last creature finally fell, the silence that followed was worse than the battle. The village was empty. There were no voices, no survivors. Just the biting cold.
Looking at the empty square, the pieces finally fell into place. The spiders did not come out of malice; they came out of starvation. The forest had been stripped of life by whatever took those animals' heads, and my poor friends were the only prey left to feed their nest.
I tracked the spiders' heavy footprints back to their mountain den, hoping against hope to recover my people before they were consumed.
Frozen Graves

When I breached the nest, my staff was raised, ready to slaughter the beasts that took my people. Instead, I found a silence thicker than the winter night.
The cavern was a slaughterhouse, but not by my hand. The massive ice spiders lay butchered across the frost alongside the remains of my villagers. The cavern floor was a lake of deep, frozen blood. My rage instantly turned into a suffocating, icy dread.

As I walked through the carnage, a chilling realization froze the breath in my lungs. Every single corpse - villager and monster alike - had been meticulously beheaded. There was not a single skull left in the den. This was not a feeding; it was a systematic harvest by something far more calculated than a mindless beast.

In the center of the gore sat an empty altar of frozen blood. Whatever rested there had been taken, but carved directly into the ice of the pedestal was a mark: a jagged, broken circle with spikes pointing toward an empty, hollow center. I do not know what this mark represents, nor do I know what kind of horror could slaughter a nest of spiders so effortlessly. I cannot let this profane site be lost to the snow. I will build my shelter directly above this den to study the symbol.

I buried my friends in headless tombs of ice, paid my final respects, and prepared for a journey. Years ago, from the hushed whispers of mercenaries, I heard tales of a profane tome - the Necronomicon - said to hold the absolute secrets of blood magic. I had long dismissed the book as a cursed relic belonging to the Dead King of the Catacombs, a place beneath my scholarly interest.
Now, it is my only lead. I will tear that book from the Catacombs if I must, for it may be the only key to understanding this cursed mark and stopping the slaughter to come.
The Throne of Death

I finally arrived at the Catacombs, a wretched domain where death holds absolute sovereignty. I carved my way through legions of the rotting dead, but my mind was numb to the battle. The image of that jagged, broken mark burned in my thoughts, denying me peace, rest, or even a breath of clear air. I had to keep moving.

In the heart of the tomb sat a corpse upon a throne, radiating a suffocating aura of decay. As I drew my staff, the bones shifted, violently rearranging themselves into a colossal, blackened skeleton: the Dead King. I fought with reckless abandon, pushing my magic to the brink. Every strike of frost was fueled by the memory of my slaughtered comrades. After what felt like days of relentless attrition, the King finally shattered.

Where his remains fell, the grimoire lay waiting. It pulsed with a sickening, heavy vitality. The Necronomicon.
The moment I touched its binding, my instincts screamed to cast it away. The power radiating from it was vile. But my vow was greater than my fear. I tore through the pages, desperate for any glimpse of the mark, only to find the cruelest of fates: the final pages had been violently ripped from the binding. On a remaining jagged edge, I caught a mere fraction of the symbol's shape.

A maddening despair washed over me. I had waded through an ocean of the dead, only to be denied the truth. But in that hollow void of failure, the tome whispered another path.
As I read its remaining pages, I uncovered magic of terrifying potency. If I could bind the raw, pulsing vitality of this blood magic to my absolute mastery over frost, I would become an unstoppable force. The magic is profane, yes, but what does morality matter in the face of annihilation? In my hands, this darkness will be forged into a weapon for a righteous hunt.
The burden of my vow has demanded a choice, and my destiny is sealed. Gripping the tome tightly, I began the long journey back to my shelter.
Ilisiitsoq
My intentions were pure. I wanted to use the Necronomicon to find true strength, to be strong enough not to have to suffer any more tragedies.

Using my ice magic, I preserved the cadavers of fallen creatures. Through the grimoire's teachings, I learned to mix blood vials with arcane ink, drawing binding runes onto the frozen flesh to stitch them together into the Tupilaqs. These undead sentinels are practically immortal; even if defeated, a drop of blood - be it human or spell-wrought - will bring them back to life. They are the perfect hunters. The grimoire warns that these thralls will turn upon a master too feeble to command them, but wielding such absolute power, I am beyond such petty concerns.

I sought out a neighboring village, eager to show them the protection I had crafted to keep them safe. I proudly presented my Tupilaqs - but the villagers did not see salvation. They saw nightmares. Their priest branded me an Ilisiitsoq, a corrupted shaman, and exiled me.
They do not understand. They are not strong enough to protect themselves from the creature from that day, but I am.

I will retreat into my sanctuary far from their sight. I will lock myself away with my Tupilaqs and guard the altar, in case the creature returns. I only have one objective now: Vengeance. Whoever - or whatever - led the massacre that day might come back, and if that happens, I'll be here waiting to take revenge, to bring peace to my comrades who died in that nest.
Lila's Secret Diary

Day 1

My name is Lila, and Papa gave me this book to celebrate my eighth winter with him. He always calls me his little miracle. He told me he found me sitting all alone in the deep snow during a terrible blizzard, not even shivering! He says he only found me because he followed a beautiful, warm light that vanished the second he picked me up. I love that story!

Papa says my imagination is too wild and I see things that aren't really there, but I just like making things more fun. I'll write about the Northern Lights that dance like spirits, and most of all, the amazing things our Angakkuq does. Marcus says that a Shaman’s job is to listen to the wind, but I think his job is mostly being a hero. I want this diary to be a treasure map of all the happy things in our village.

Day 3

The snow was so deep today! I tried to help Papa with the sled, but I fell in and looked like a giant snowball. Marcus saw me and laughed, but then he used his magic to make the snow stand up and shape itself. He built a snowman that looked exactly like Papa, complete with a funny ice-sculpted nose!

I clapped and told him I love tricks like that - playing with the looks of things is so fun! With enough effort you can make even a scary wolf look like a playful puppy. He just smiled, patted my head, and said his magic is only meant to keep us safe. I want to be a master of frost just like him one day, so I can play games with the snow!

Day 6

I was playing near the tree line today and met a new friend. He’s very tall, very quiet, and a bit clumsy because he lost something super important to him. He was looking everywhere in the snow! I told him I would help him find it, but only if he played a game with me first.

Later, I saw Marcus. He has been patrolling a lot lately, and his eyes look so worried. I asked him if the monsters are coming, and he just patted my head and said, 'Not while I’m standing, Lila.' I want to make him smile again. I’m going to spend the whole evening working on a special surprise for him. I hope the blue thread matches his robes.

Day 13

I finished it! It’s a bit small, but it’s the warmest hat in the village. I used the special wool Papa brought back from the coast. It took so much careful planning to get every piece exactly right! Marcus does so much for everyone—he guards us from the dark and uses his frost to build tall walls that block the biting wind.

Tomorrow morning, I’m going to run to the village square and give it to him before he starts his patrol. I can’t wait to see his face when he sees my surprise! I just know it's going to change everything.
The Last Grave

I have finished the last of the graves. My hands are numb, not from the cold, but from the weight of the silence.
To those who come after: do not mourn the man I was, for he died in this cavern alongside his kin. The man who leaves today is a shadow, driven only by a promise and the hope to find answers.

I cannot stop looking at the mark on the altar. Every time I close my eyes, I see it burnt into the back of my eyelids.
I am heading for the Catacombs. I need answers for this massacre, and there’s no better place to search for them than the place where the Necronomicon was created.
If you are reading this, and I have not returned, let the frost take these tombs. Let the snow bury my name. But whatever you do... do not get involved with the mark.
Evil in the Forest

The traps are empty again, but it’s not because the game has moved on. The forest is dead quiet. No birds, no howling, nothing.
Yesterday, I found a dire wolf in one of my snares. Or, at least, most of it. The head was gone. It wasn't torn off by a bear or bitten clean through by a spider; the cut was perfectly smooth, like it was done by a blade sharper than any I've seen.

I went further up the ridge to track whatever did it. I found a massive tree deep in the pines. Carved into the bark, deep enough to bleed sap, was a symbol: a jagged circle with spikes pointing inward. My blood ran cold the moment I looked at it. I am packing up my gear tonight. Whatever is claiming the beasts of this forest is not natural, and I refuse to be its next trophy.
Heresy

May the spirits forgive us, for we have banished one of our own.
Marcus of the northern peaks came to us yesterday, claiming he held the key to our salvation against a nameless dread. But what followed him into our square was an affront to life itself. He paraded grotesque amalgams of frozen, rotting flesh, stitched together with profane runes and smelling of old blood. He called them his 'Tupilaqs'—protectors.
I saw no protection in those lifeless, hollow eyes. I saw only the corruption of the grave.

When I ordered him to destroy them, he looked at me not with the wisdom of an Angakkuq, but with the manic, hollow stare of a madman. He clutched a strange, pulsing egg to his chest and cursed us for our blindness. I have officially branded him an Ilisiitsoq. He is dead to us now. I only pray that his dark magic stays in the wastes, for if those stitched horrors ever turn hungry, God help us all.
lore.magic_realms.world_1.title: I. The Age of Monsters and the Divine Bet
lore.magic_realms.world_1.unlock:
Long ago, the overworld belonged entirely to Monsters.
Above them, in a realm untouched by the chaos below, lived the Gods. However, these supreme beings suffered from eternal boredom, finding the primal, mindless state of the world deeply unamusing.
To entertain themselves, the Gods held a council and voted to introduce a new, intelligent species to the board: humans. 
Gods agreed this would be a major improvement to the world, but established one unbreakable rule: humans were to live freely, and the Gods were strictly forbidden from killing them directly.
Because frail humans could not survive the harsh environment, the Gods granted a select few the ability to control mana. The Gods watched humans develop with intense satisfaction.
lore.magic_realms.world_2.title: II. The Spark of Rebellion and the Divine Schism
lore.magic_realms.world_2.unlock:
The entertainment turned to unease when humanity achieved the impossible: without any divine help, they discovered a method to awaken mana in the humans who were born without it.
This revelation sent shockwaves through the divine realm. The Gods realized their experiment was growing too powerful and slipping from their control. The divine realm fractured into two bitterly opposed factions: 
The Preservationists, who wanted to maintain the pact.
The Eradicators, who wanted to break the pact and end the experiment entirely.
As tensions boiled over, the Gods became entirely consumed by their own internal, philosophical warfare, taking their eyes off the overworld.
lore.magic_realms.world_3.title: III. The Order of the Veiled Eye and the Great Disappearance
lore.magic_realms.world_3.unlock:
During the Gods' distraction, the original, most powerful human mages unlocked a forbidden discipline: the Magic of Foresight. They gazed into the future and realized the catastrophic danger this magic posed. If it spread, it would cause the extinction of humanity.
To protect the secrets of humanity, the original human mages formed The Order of the Veiled Eye. Using their foresight, the Order witnessed the Eradicator Gods targeting them. Fearing the imminent fall of their kind, the most powerful mages of the Order erased their tracks and went into hiding, isolating themselves from the rest of the world.
lore.magic_realms.world_4.title: IV. The Loophole and the Hollow Crown
lore.magic_realms.world_4.unlock:
When the Gods finally turned their attention back to the overworld, the greatest human mages had vanished. The Preservationist Gods assumed the monsters had simply overrun them. The Eradicators suspected foul play, but lacking proof, and seeing that the remaining humans were weak and ordinary, they lost their argument to intervene directly.
Feigning agreement, the Eradicators secretly crafted a plan to wipe out humanity without breaking the sacred pact. Their plan centers on the Hollow Crown, a dark mark that feeds the ancient beast Skallhöggr with the skulls of the fallen, with the objective of granting him enough strength to devour humanity.

message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_tip.1: %s I've heard rumours about a book called Necronomicon that has information regarding blood magic, things like blood pacts and other kind of cursed rituals.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_tip.2: %s Some of the mercenaries that visit this tavern have very weird quirks. The other day a mercenary with a bookworm quirk arrived carrying some books with him, and he seemed unusually fast.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_tip.3: %s Did you know that contracted mercenaries can perform better or worse depending on their personalities? For example, i once saw two arrogant contracted mercenaries fighting together and they seemed weaker and slower than usual.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_tip.4: %s Someone once dropped hundreds of TnT carts at the tavern, it was such a mess and the tavern got completely destroyed, so I couldn't offer the tavern services anymore.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_tip.5: %s Want to hear something funny? If you put any living thing in a close space with 500 wolves, it will die instantly. Don't ask me how do I know that.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_tip.6: %s I've heard rumours about a blood spell that can be used to strip immortality from mercenaries, but no one has ever confirmed it.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_no_tips: %s Sorry but we don't have any information available right now.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_welcome1: %s Ale’s cheap, gossip’s free, and the chairs only bite if you kick them first.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_welcome2: %s Ah, travelers! Come inside, leave your troubles at the door and your coin at the bar.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_welcome3: %s Welcome weary souls! The fire’s warm, the ale’s strong, and the beds only mildly haunted.
message.magic_realms.tavernkeep_farewell: %s Try not to die before your next visit, we’re running a loyalty program!
%s Don’t forget your tab - oh wait, you didn’t pay it.
%s Safe roads, friend. May your coin purse stay heavy and your path well-lit.

message.magic_realms.eden.special_phrase: %s Did you know i once fought the Tavernkeeper? He sure was strong, and he told me that I was the first human to defeat him.

message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.defau: %s Nothing beats a quiet morning by the water.
%s Fishing? I've caught a few in my time.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.cheer: %s Oh, I LOVE fishing! Best catch of my life was a salmon as long as my arm!
%s A day by the lake? Count me in!
%s Fished once. Caught a boot. Never again.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.schol: %s Did you know salmon can remember their birth stream for years? Fascinating.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.defau: %s The fish aren't biting today. Just need to wait.
%s Sometimes the best part of fishing is catching absolutely nothing.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.cheer: %s Did you see the one that jumped over there?! Oh, this is so exciting!
%s I just love looking at all the colorful fish before I throw them back!
%s The depths are cold and unforgiving. Much like the rest of this world.
%s Another dead thing pulled from the water.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.schol: %s By observing the insect activity on the surface, we can predict the feeding patterns of the local aquatic life.
%s I'm currently cataloging the freshwater species of this region. Fascinating biodiversity.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.arrog: %s I don't use bait. True masters catch salmon with their bare hands.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.cowar: %s Y-you don't think there are any... sea monsters down there, do you?
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.greed: %s I heard they found a sunken treasure ship near here. Keep your eyes on the hooks!
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.hothe: %s If this stupid fish steals my bait one more time, I'm diving in after it!
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.jovia: %s Ho! We've got a fighter on the line! This calls for a celebration!
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.loyal: %s I promised the squad a fish dinner tonight. I won't let them down.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.pious: %s The rivers are the veins of the earth, providing bounty to those who respect them.
message.magic_realms.hobby.fishing.super: %s Never bring bananas on a fishing boat. It's terrible luck.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.defau: %s History always has lessons, if you know where to look.
%s Old ruins, old bones, old stories.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.schol: %s The archives at Kingsreach have texts going back six hundred years - truly priceless.
%s Every ruin is a library if you have the patience to read it.
%s I could talk about the Third Dynasty for hours. You sure you want me to start?
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.super: %s Some old places are best left alone. The dead don't always stay quiet.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.jovia: %s Ah, history! Full of drunks and fools and kings - usually the same people.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.defau: %s Every kingdom falls eventually. It's the way of the world.
%s Artifacts tell the stories that people forget.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.schol: %s My dissertation covers the socio-economic collapse of the Second Empire. It's a riveting read.
%s Notice the masonry here? This predates the Cataclysm by at least two centuries.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.super: %s These ruins are cursed. The history books won't tell you that, but the locals know.
%s The ancients dug too deep, and awoke something terrible. We must not repeat their mistakes.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.jovia: %s Did you know the famous King Aldous was actually terrified of geese? History is hilarious!
%s Let's raise a glass to the heroes of old! Even if half their stories are exaggerated!
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.arrog: %s When history books are written about this era, my name will be on every page.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.cheer: %s I love reading about ancient festivals! They threw the best parties back then!
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.cowar: %s E-everyone who lived here is dead... let's just go back to the tavern.
%s History is nothing but a long, unbroken record of war, famine, and betrayal.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.loyal: %s We honor the traditions of our ancestors. To forget them is to lose our identity.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.pious: %s The holy texts have guided our civilization for millennia. History is the study of faith.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.greed: %s The only good thing about history is all the buried treasure those dead kings left behind.
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.hothe: %s I don't care who fought who a hundred years ago! Who are we fighting NOW?!
message.magic_realms.hobby.history.stoic: %s Empires rise, empires fall. We must simply endure what comes.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.default: %s A good tune makes the road shorter.
%s I can carry a note, mostly.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.cheerfu: %s Music! Oh, I know a hundred tavern songs - want to hear one?
%s Nothing raises spirits like a good chorus around the fire!
%s Play something, anything! I'll drink and sing along.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.stoic.0: %s I prefer silence. But the right song, played right... I'll listen.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.default: %s Plucking a lute is a fine way to pass the evening.
%s A heavy heart needs a light melody.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.cheerfu: %s La la la! Come on, everyone sing with me! You know the words!
%s Fast tempos make me want to dance until my feet hurt!
%s *Bangs mug on table* That's the spirit! Play 'The Drunken Creeper' next!
%s My voice is terrible, but I sing loudly anyway! Hahaha!
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.stoic.1: %s The drums keep the marching pace. Crucial for discipline.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.stoic.2: %s A low hum is enough. Anything more is a distraction.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.arrogan: %s Your timing is completely off. Give me that instrument, let a true virtuoso play.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.cowardl: %s Shh! P-play quieter! You'll attract monsters with all that noise!
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.grim.1: %s Play a requiem. It suits the mood of this wretched land.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.hothead: %s That's not how the song goes! You're ruining it! Play it faster!
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.scholar: %s The acoustics in this cavern amplify the C-minor chord beautifully.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.pious.1: %s Let us lift our voices in hymns, to praise the light that guides us.
%s I know a beautiful ballad, but it'll cost you a silver piece to hear it.
message.magic_realms.hobby.music.loyal.0: %s This is the marching song of my old regiment. I sing it to remember them.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.defa: %s A fair game now and then keeps the blood moving.
%s I've won some, lost more. That's how it goes.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.gree: %s Care for a round of dice? Wager's your choice.
%s Easy gold is still gold, my friend.
%s The house always wins... unless you ARE the house.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.piou: %s The dice are a sin, they say. I say the gods enjoy a good bet themselves.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.supe: %s Never gamble on a Tuesday. Never. I learned that the hard way.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.defa: %s Just one more toss of the dice.
%s You have to know when to walk away.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.gree: %s Double or nothing! Come on, I know my luck is turning around!
%s Look at all those shiny coins... soon they'll all be in my pouch.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.piou: %s I only play for copper, and any winnings go to the temple.
%s Do not let the allure of gold corrupt your soul, my friend.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.supe: %s I blew on the dice, tapped the table three times, and crossed my fingers. I can't lose.
%s I drew the Tower card today. I'm not placing any bets until tomorrow.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.arro: %s You honestly think you can beat me at cards? How amusing.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.chee: %s Oh, I lost again! Haha! Well, it's just a game, right?
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.cowa: %s P-please don't make me bet my boots. I need them.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.grim: %s We gamble with our lives every day. What does a few coins matter?
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.hoth: %s You cheated! I saw you slip that card from your sleeve! Draw your blade!
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.jovi: %s Hah! A royal flush! The drinks are on me tonight!
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.scho: %s Based on the cards played, the probability of you holding a winning hand is exactly 12.4%. I call.
message.magic_realms.hobby.gambling.loya: %s I would never bet against my own squad. That's bad luck and bad form.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.de: %s The sky's always been the same. We just tell different stories about it.
%s Clear nights are a gift. Don't waste them.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.sc: %s The Wanderer's Lamp - that bright one - shifts three degrees every century. Imagine that.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.su: %s A falling star means someone was born. Or died. I never remember which.
%s When the red moon rises, lock your doors. That's all I'll say.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.pi: %s The heavens were written by a hand we'll never understand. I find that comforting.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.gr: %s Stars are just distant fires. Ours will go out someday too.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.de: %s Looking up makes you realize how small we really are.
%s Finding the North Star is the first thing a traveler should learn.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.sc: %s I'm calculating the orbital trajectory of that comet. It should return in exactly 74 years.
%s The constellations are ancient navigation tools, not magical omens.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.su: %s The stars are restless tonight. The spirits are trying to send us a warning.
%s Do not point directly at a shooting star, or it will steal your luck!
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.pi: %s The night sky is a grand tapestry woven by the divine.
%s Every star is a righteous soul watching over us from the heavens.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.gr: %s Starlight is just an illusion. The darkness between the stars is the only truth.
%s We are nothing but dust beneath a cold, unfeeling cosmos.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.ar: %s I was born under the sign of the Conqueror. Greatness was my destiny.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.ch: %s Wow! The sky looks like it's covered in glitter! How beautiful!
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.co: %s It's too dark to see the stars properly... and the darkness is where the zombies hide.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.jo: %s That constellation right there? Looks exactly like a giant mug of ale to me!
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.gr: %s If those stars were made of diamonds, I'd build a ladder to the sky.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.ho: %s Why are we just sitting around looking at the sky?! We're wasting time!
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.lo: %s I promised my old commander I'd look up at the North Star every night. I keep my promises.
message.magic_realms.hobby.stargazing.st: %s The stars do not care about our struggles. It is a comforting constant.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.defau: %s A good meal is half the reason I get out of bed.
%s Salt, fire, patience. That's most of it.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.jovia: %s Cooking? I ONCE fed twenty men on one rabbit and a jug of wine. Legend!
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.cheer: %s I love the way a kitchen smells. Nothing like it!
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.schol: %s The Maillard reaction - that's what browns meat. Chemistry on a plate.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.defau: %s Chop the carrots, dice the potatoes... the rhythm is relaxing.
%s You can tell a lot about someone by how they season their stew.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.cheer: %s I made extra pastries! Who wants a sweet roll?!
%s Baking is just magic you can eat! I love it so much!
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.jovia: %s More butter! More wine! If the pan isn't sizzling, you're not trying!
%s A good feast cures any wound! Grab a plate, my friend!
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.schol: %s If you substitute crushed blaze powder for pepper, the culinary applications are endless, though mildly explosive.
%s The exact boiling point of this broth will determine the tenderness of the meat. Precision is key.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.arrog: %s My culinary genius is wasted on mercenaries who wouldn't know a truffle from dirt.
%s Do not touch my ingredients. You will only ruin the masterpiece I am preparing.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.greed: %s I only use the finest golden apples in my recipes. It shows off my wealth and my taste.
%s Rations. Hardtack. It's fuel for the body, nothing more. Stop whining about the flavor.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.hothe: %s Who turned down the heat on my cauldron?! I said rolling boil!
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.loyal: %s I make sure my comrades are well-fed. An empty stomach makes for a weak shield line.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.pious: %s We bless this harvest before it goes into the pot. To waste it is a sin.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.super: %s Always stir clockwise. Counter-clockwise invites malicious spirits into the soup.
message.magic_realms.hobby.cooking.cowar: %s P-please don't make me chop the onions... the knife is so sharp, I might slip!
title.magic_realms.bane_of_the_dead.desc: 250 undead put back in the ground.
title.magic_realms.veteran.desc: A thousand kills and still standing.
title.magic_realms.hell_walker.desc: Walked the fortresses and bastions of the Nether.
title.magic_realms.unbroken.desc: Has taken everything the world could throw.
title.magic_realms.archmage.desc: Mastery of the arcane, proven against the mighty.
title.magic_realms.axemaster.desc: Four hundred kills, and the axe never dulled.
title.magic_realms.bowyer.desc: Death arrives before the sound does.
title.magic_realms.mace_lord.desc: The mace answers to no one else.
title.magic_realms.godbane.desc: First person to defeat a creature that doesn't belong to this realm.
title.magic_realms.nature_lover.desc: Nature magic loves her as much as she loves nature.
title.magic_realms.mushroom_lover.desc: By eating so many mushrooms, he almost turns into one.
title.magic_realms.retainer.desc: Two hours in your service, and still here.
title.magic_realms.vermin_culler.desc: Nothing with that many legs frightens them now.
title.magic_realms.raidbreaker.desc: Has stood where the horns sounded, and held.
title.magic_realms.bonepicker.desc: Knows exactly where a skeleton comes apart.
title.magic_realms.voidwalker.desc: Met their stare too many times to flinch.
title.magic_realms.tidebound.desc: The deep let them go. It rarely does.
title.magic_realms.mansion_ghost.desc: Walked those halls uninvited and unnoticed.
title.magic_realms.trialborn.desc: The chambers tested them and found no fault.
title.magic_realms.hearthguard.desc: Known by name in five villages.
title.magic_realms.juggernaut.desc: Ten thousand blows and still walking.
title.magic_realms.relentless.desc: The arm has never once been tired.
title.magic_realms.deathless.desc: Fifteen times it should have ended. It didn't.
title.magic_realms.swordmaster.desc: The blade is no longer a separate thing.
title.magic_realms.giantslayer.desc: Three of the great ones, felled.
title.magic_realms.paragon.desc: There is nothing left to prove.
title.magic_realms.sapper.desc: Learned to stand still when the hissing starts.
title.magic_realms.tomb_robber.desc: The old vaults gave up what they were hiding.

subtitles.magic_realms.order_lore_2: The Order of the Veiled Eye: Log 2
